rfm_tuples.R: Same-store sales — Jack in the Box: Company 0.0%, Franchise (1.5)%, System (1.3)% for FY24; Del Taco: Company (1.3)%, Franchise (1.6)%, System (1.5)% for FY24. Jack in the Box company SSS 0.0% = +3.4% average check (incl. 7.4% pricing) MINUS 3.4% transactions; Del Taco company SSS (1.3)% = +4.2% average check (incl. 7.3% pricing) MINUS 5.5% transactions.
rfm_tuples.f: Traffic-vs-price decomposition: assess whether headline SSS is masking pure traffic erosion. The 7.4% Jack price + (3.4%) traffic and 7.3% Del Taco price + (5.5%) traffic shows guest-count collapse offset only by aggressive menu pricing — a classic late-cycle QSR distress signal.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Both brands: pricing absorbed at 7.3–7.4% (well above CPI food-away-from-home) yet traffic still down 3.4% (Jack) and 5.5% (Del Taco). Magnitude of traffic decline at Del Taco is severe; Jack masked flat headline.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 'flat' Jack in the Box company SSS is functionally a traffic-driven down-comp papered over by 7.4% pricing — a non-repeatable lever. Del Taco company traffic down 5.5% on top of 7.3% price is a leading indicator of demand destruction and franchisee P&L stress. Disclosure is technically accurate but the narrative pillar ('flat SSS') obscures a deteriorating unit economic picture.

rfm_tuples.R: 'In fiscal year 2024, we continued our refranchising strategy with three main intentions. First, to create a company-wide asset-light model that will benefit from mitigating exposure to macroeconomic pressures; second, to generate incremental development agreements throughout the refranchising process that provide a more robust unit growth pipeline than otherwise achievable; and third, to provide a more efficient capital structure. … We refranchised 47 Del Taco restaurants in fiscal year 2024, and 111 Del Taco restaurants in 2023. In connection with the 2024 refranchising, we added 42 new development commitments.'
rfm_tuples.f: Refranchising velocity & pricing check: compare unit-level proceeds and gains-on-sale to the 'asset-light, robust unit growth pipeline' framing. Look for proceeds-per-unit deterioration.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24: 47 Del Taco refranchised, proceeds $19.4M from sale of company-operated restaurants, gains of $3.3M. FY23: 116 units refranchised (111 Del Taco + 5 Jack), proceeds $85.2M, gains $18.0M. Per-unit proceeds: ~$413K (FY24) vs ~$735K (FY23) — proceeds-per-unit dropped ~44%. Refranchising pace also slowed (47 vs 111).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Refranchising velocity halved and per-unit proceeds collapsed ~44% YoY — the opposite of what 'incremental development agreements' and 'asset-light' framing implies. The deal economics deteriorated materially, consistent with weaker franchisee bidder appetite for Del Taco units. The 42 new development commitments are forward promises, not realized deals.

rfm_tuples.R: 'During the third quarter of 2024, the Company identified triggering events that indicated the goodwill allocated to the Del Taco reporting unit might be impaired. … the Company performed a quantitative test … noting that the fair value of the reporting unit was less than the carrying value, which resulted in an impairment of goodwill of $162.6 million.' Goodwill balance per balance sheet collapsed from $329.986M (FY23) to $161.209M (FY24). The KPMG critical audit matter cites Del Taco goodwill of only $25.4M remaining.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B: derive the trajectory. A $162.6M impairment 2.5 years after the $585M Del Taco acquisition (March 2022) — implies further impairment risk is non-trivial. Test claim consistency between MD&A optimism and the impairment magnitude.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Del Taco acquired March 2022 for ~$585M cash. Through FY24 the Del Taco reporting unit has experienced significant goodwill writedowns ($162.6M in FY24 alone). KPMG flagged Del Taco goodwill valuation as the SOLE critical audit matter and noted revenue growth rate assumptions as 'challenging to evaluate.' Del Taco SSS trajectory remains negative going into FY25.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The Del Taco acquisition is functionally repudiated by the impairment. Management continues to describe 'robust unit growth pipeline' and 'asset-light' optimism in the same filing where the auditor singled out Del Taco goodwill valuation as the critical audit matter. The combination of (i) negative comps, (ii) per-unit refranchise economics dropping 44%, and (iii) auditor highlighting revenue growth rate assumptions as the single area of subjective judgment is a high-probability further-impairment setup.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Under the Indenture, the Master Issuer has approximately $1.7 billion of outstanding debt as of September 29, 2024.' Long-term debt $1,699.4M + current maturities $35.9M = ~$1.735B total. Class A-2-I Notes ($550M, 3.445%) have an anticipated repayment date of February 2027; Class A-2-II Notes ($550M, 4.136%) February 2032. 'The quarterly principal payment on the Class A-2 Notes may be suspended when the specified leverage ratio … is less than or equal to 5.0x.'
rfm_tuples.f: Capital structure / refinancing wall: locate the 2027 ARD relative to cutoff (May 2025) and check whether the leverage trajectory is improving or worsening. Note: securitized debt with anticipated repayment dates triggers rapid amortization if not refinanced.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Refinancing wall: $550M Class A-2-I (Series 2022-1) due Feb 2027 (~21 months after cutoff). Cash $24.7M + restricted $29.4M = $54.2M total cash; available borrowings $169.5M between VFN and revolver. FY24 operating cash flow collapsed to $68.8M from $215.0M (down 68%). Interest expense $82.1M consumes ~120% of FY24 op cash flow.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: $54M cash against a $550M 2027 maturity with operating cash flow that dropped 68% YoY and now barely covers interest. The 'we expect cash flows … will be sufficient … for the foreseeable future' framing is technically true at the 12-month horizon but materially obscures the 21-month refinancing wall under deteriorating credit-spread/comp-trajectory conditions. The fact that the securitization itself can trigger rapid amortization if DSCR slips makes the leverage trajectory the central forward risk.

rfm_tuples.R: 'In fiscal 2024, the Company repurchased 1.1 million shares of its common stock for an aggregate cost of $70.6 million … As of September 29, 2024, there was $180.0 million remaining under share repurchase programs.' Quarterly dividends of $0.44/share totaling $34.2M. 'On August 16, 2024, the Company adopted a Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement to repurchase shares of the Company s common stock up to an aggregate purchase price of $15.0 million. This Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement subsequently terminated on September 27, 2024.'
rfm_tuples.f: Capital-action sanity check vs cash trajectory and pending impairment. Buyback + dividend totaled $104.8M while operating cash flow was only $68.8M — capital return EXCEEDED organic cash generation. Mode-B: a 10b5-1 plan adopted Aug 16 and terminated Sept 27 (only 6 weeks) is a highly unusual signal.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Buyback $70.6M + Dividends $34.2M = $104.8M capital return. Operating cash flow $68.8M. Shortfall funded out of cash (net cash dropped $131.7M FY24). 10b5-1 buyback plan adopted Aug 16, 2024 → terminated Sept 27, 2024 — a ~6-week life, terminated 2 days before fiscal year-end and ~2 months before goodwill impairment was finalized in the 10-K.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Two issues compound: (1) capital return exceeded operating cash flow by $36M during a year of negative SSS, $162.6M goodwill impairment, and a 21-month refinancing wall — a misallocation of scarce liquidity. (2) The very short-lived 10b5-1 plan (6 weeks, terminated just before fiscal year-end) is unusual; the typical purpose of 10b5-1 plans is multi-month/quarter execution. Termination immediately before an FY-end with a material impairment to be disclosed is the textbook insider-vs-calendar pattern Mode B is supposed to catch.

rfm_tuples.R: Total stockholders deficit of ($851.8M) at FY24-end, widened from ($718.3M) at FY23-end. Treasury stock $3,195.6M (a $70.6M increase from $3,125.0M reflecting FY24 buybacks). Retained earnings $1,866.7M (decreased from $1,937.6M due to net loss and dividends).
rfm_tuples.f: Balance sheet stress check: in a securitized capital structure with negative book equity, every dollar of buyback widens stockholders deficit and reduces the cushion for distressed-debt holders. Test consistency with management's 'asset-light, efficient capital structure' framing.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Stockholders deficit widened $133.5M YoY (from -$718.3M to -$851.8M). Net loss $36.7M + dividends $34.2M + buybacks $70.6M + actuarial losses $5.7M = $147.2M drain (vs $133.5M widening; rounding/share-based comp explains delta). The company has cumulatively bought back $3.2B of stock over its history while operating cash flow is now collapsing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Continued buybacks into a widening stockholders deficit during a year of operating distress is governance-flagging. Not unusual for securitized franchisors, but the magnitude relative to cash flow makes it acute. The 'efficient capital structure' narrative is in tension with the actual trajectory.

rfm_tuples.R: '(1) Effective November 20, 2024, Brian Scott is departing the company to pursue a new position outside the restaurant industry. Dawn Hooper, the Company s Senior Vice President, Controller, will serve as the Company s interim principal financial officer effective November 1, 2024, and as Interim Chief Financial Officer effective upon Brian Scott s departure and until the Company s new Chief Financial Officer, Lance Tucker, begins his employment on January 13, 2025.' Scott had been CFO only 1 year per the executive officer table.
rfm_tuples.f: CFO turnover proximate to filing date and major impairment. The 10-K was signed November 21, 2024 by interim CFO Dawn Hooper; CFO Brian Scott departed November 20 — literally the day before the 10-K signing. Mode-B: CFO turnover proximate to first-ever goodwill impairment is a classic forensic signal.
rfm_tuples.M_value: CFO Brian Scott (tenure: 1 year) departed Nov 20, 2024 — one day before 10-K filing date Nov 21, 2024. The 10-K is signed by Interim CFO Dawn Hooper. Permanent CFO Lance Tucker not starting until Jan 13, 2025. This is the SECOND consecutive year-end with material C-suite churn. No 'disagreement with auditors' (Item 9 = None) but the timing is striking. KPMG is the auditor since 1986 (long-tenure, low rotation risk).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: CFO departure the day before the 10-K is signed, after only 1 year tenure, coinciding with a $162.6M goodwill impairment and the first net loss in years — this is the canonical CFO-exit-around-bad-news pattern. The 10-K is being signed by an interim with no permanent CFO in place at filing. This dramatically increases probability of further write-downs and accounting cleanup in fiscal 2025 under the new CFO.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Royalties as a percentage of total franchise restaurant sales (1) 5.0% [FY24] vs 5.2% [FY23] … (1) Excluding the impact of the $7.3 million termination fee in the first quarter of the prior year, royalties as a percentage of total franchised restaurant sales would be 5.0% for the fiscal year ended October 1, 2023.' 'Franchise support and other costs increased $2.7 million, or 26.4% in 2024, mainly related to a $2.0 million increase in bad debt expense due to a rollover of a bad debt reversal in the prior year.'
rfm_tuples.f: Franchisee health canary: bad debt expense direction + royalty rate sensitivity to one-time termination fees. Mode-B: a 26.4% jump in franchise support costs with $2.0M of bad debt is a leading indicator of franchisee financial stress.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Jack in the Box: franchise royalties $198.4M (FY24) vs $207.1M (FY23), down 4.2%, driven partly by 'lower royalty income driven by lower sales.' Franchise support costs +26.4% YoY with $2.0M bad debt swing. Del Taco franchise costs as % of revenue went from 63.7% to 72.0% — an 8.3pp deterioration in franchise unit economics for the franchisor.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The franchise support cost spike and bad debt swing are leading indicators of franchisee financial distress (particularly in CA where AB 1228 raised wages 25%+ for QSR workers in April 2024 and where 70% of the system is concentrated). Del Taco franchise costs/revenue deteriorated 8.3pp YoY. These are early warning signs that the refranchising 'pipeline' will face headwinds and that royalty revenue (the high-margin annuity) is under pressure.

rfm_tuples.R: 'approximately 70% of our systemwide restaurants are located in the states of California and Texas. Economic conditions, state and local laws, or government regulations affecting those states may therefore more greatly impact our results than would similar occurrences in other locations.' California-specific: 'AB 1228, which went into effect April 2024, have raised labor costs, particularly given our high concentration of restaurants in California.'
rfm_tuples.f: Geographic concentration: per the Properties table, California has 946 Jack in the Box and 355 Del Taco restaurants = 1,301 of 2,785 total = 47% in California alone. Test for AB 1228 wage cost run-rate and margin trajectory.
rfm_tuples.M_value: AB 1228 (CA $20 QSR minimum wage) effective April 1, 2024 — only 6 months of impact in FY24 financial. Jack in the Box payroll +0.7pp to 31.5% of company restaurant sales (wage inflation 6.9%). Del Taco payroll +2.7pp to 36.7% (wage inflation 9.7%). FY25 will have a full 12 months of AB 1228 impact PLUS another April 2025 step-up if applicable. CA = 47% of system; full-year run-rate impact is materially worse than disclosed FY24 partial-year impact.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: FY24 only captures 6 months of AB 1228 ($20/hr CA QSR minimum). The FY25 run-rate margin impact will be roughly 2x what is shown, and there is no offsetting price lever left (already at 7.4% Jack/7.3% Del Taco pricing with traffic declining 3.4–5.5%). The 'asset-light' refranchising narrative is partly a response to this margin reality but does not solve it for the 7%/22% company-operated remaining footprint.

This is a coverage gap, not a finding. Recommendation: fetch any 10-Q filed between 2024-11-21 and 2025-05-15 for JACK and rerun this tuple.

supplemental_signals.auditor_history: KPMG since 1986 (no change, long-tenure auditor); unqualified opinion on FY24 financials; critical audit matter = Del Taco goodwill (signals further-impairment risk)
supplemental_signals.going_concern: No going concern language. Management asserts 12-month liquidity sufficient. But $54M cash vs $550M 2027 refinancing wall + 68% YoY operating cash flow decline is materially obscured by 12-month-horizon framing.
supplemental_signals.cfo_turnover: Brian Scott departed Nov 20, 2024 — ONE DAY before 10-K filed Nov 21, 2024. Tenure: 1 year. Interim CFO Dawn Hooper signed 10-K. Permanent replacement Lance Tucker started Jan 13, 2025.
supplemental_signals.10b5_1_anomaly: Company adopted 10b5-1 buyback plan Aug 16, 2024 → terminated Sept 27, 2024 (6-week life, terminated 2 days before fiscal year-end and ~2 months before goodwill impairment was disclosed in 10-K)
supplemental_signals.geographic_concentration: 47% of system in California (1,301/2,785 units) — full-year AB 1228 wage impact starting FY25
supplemental_signals.del_taco_acquisition_repudiation: Del Taco acquired March 2022 for ~$585M; $162.6M goodwill impairment FY24; remaining Del Taco goodwill only $25.4M per KPMG critical audit matter; same-store sales negative; per-unit refranchise proceeds dropped 44% YoY
supplemental_signals.capital_return_vs_cashflow: Buyback $70.6M + Dividends $34.2M = $104.8M return vs $68.8M operating cash flow — net cash dropped $131.7M FY24
supplemental_signals.stockholders_deficit: Widened from ($718.3M) to ($851.8M) — buybacks into a deficit during operational distress
supplemental_signals.securitized_debt_wall: $550M Class A-2-I Notes ARD Feb 2027; rapid amortization triggers tied to DSCR, gross sales floors, and refinancing failure

summary: JACK exhibits the classic late-cycle leveraged-franchisor distress signature with five reinforcing red flags: (1) traffic-driven SSS decline at both brands papered over by 7.3-7.4% pricing that cannot be repeated; (2) Del Taco acquisition functionally repudiated via $162.6M goodwill impairment with KPMG flagging the remaining $25.4M as the sole critical audit matter; (3) refranchising velocity halved while per-unit proceeds dropped 44% YoY despite 'robust pipeline' narrative; (4) capital return ($104.8M) exceeded operating cash flow ($68.8M) while stockholders deficit widened $133M against a $550M 2027 securitized refinancing wall with only $54M cash; (5) CFO departed the day before the 10-K was signed, with a short-lived 10b5-1 buyback plan terminated 2 days before fiscal year-end and 2 months before the impairment disclosure. The filing is technically compliant (no going concern, unqualified KPMG opinion) but uses 12-month liquidity framing, 'asset-light' rhetoric, and headline 'flat' Jack SSS to obscure a deteriorating franchise system facing full-year AB 1228 wage step-up in FY25. Strong SHORT signal under the honesty-alpha framework: the disclosures are accurate but the narrative pillars are unsustainable.
